summary: Next.js App Router pages and route handlers that compose the Barkpark web demo: a split-view document finder with an interactive corpus graph, scoped workspace/project browsing, SSE live-listen proxying, and unified document detail rendering across all content types.

intentions.title: Deliver a split-view finder UX where search state survives document navigation
intentions.evidence: (finder)/layout.tsx mounts <Finder> in the layout shell (not per-page) so it never remounts; server-seeds the initial browse; (finder)/page.tsx and d/[type]/[slug]/page.tsx are the two children slots that swap without disturbing the left rail

intentions.title: Visualise the content corpus as an interactive graph on the landing screen
intentions.evidence: (finder)/page.tsx fetches fetchCorpusGraph and renders <GraphLanding>; document node clicks navigate inside the finder route group preserving sidebar state; mobile gets a fallback hint

intentions.title: Proxy the private SSE live-listen stream safely to the browser
intentions.evidence: v1/data/listen/[dataset]/route.ts injects BARKPARK_READ_TOKEN server-side, forwards Last-Event-ID, pipes text/event-stream with X-Accel-Buffering:no so the browser subscribes same-origin with no token exposed

intentions.title: Support multi-tenant workspace/project scoping with graceful degradation
intentions.evidence: w/[workspace]/p/[project]/layout.tsx builds a workspace+project switcher from listWorkspaces/listProjects, falls back to static label on fetch failure; scoped client is built per-request in nested pages

intentions.title: Unified document detail route covering all content types (posts, papers, sheets, media, …)
intentions.evidence: d/[type]/[slug]/page.tsx maintains KNOWN_TYPES set, issues real HTTP 404 for unknown types via notFound(), uses ISR with on-demand revalidation via unstable_cache+revalidateTag

intentions.title: Demonstrate SDK consumption patterns (raw fetch, @barkpark/nextjs, live) as a living reference
intentions.evidence: web/AGENTS.md declares the app is the 'read-only Next.js demo consuming the Phoenix API'; route handlers, scoped client, and live proxy together exercise every major SDK surface
